A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ringmaster ASGD work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: Appendix F and Figure 2 report the authors' simulated quadratic-optimization experiment comparing Ringmaster ASGD, Delay-Adaptive ASGD, and Rennala SGD.

after.justification: Appendix G retains the original quadratic comparison, and Appendix G.1 adds MNIST neural-network training results in Figure 3.

M1.justification: Algorithms 3–5 retain their update procedures. Section 4.1 adds an optional threshold-selection rule, R=max{σ sqrt(m*/ε),1}, with m* depending on worker computation times, alongside the retained universal threshold. This is a limited parameter-selection extension; its use in the experiments is not established.

E1.justification: v1's original evaluation uses a synthetic convex quadratic problem. v2 retains it and adds MNIST neural-network training in Appendix G.1, substantially extending coverage to optimization of a neural model on real image data.

E2.justification: The quadratic comparison retains Rennala SGD and Delay-Adaptive ASGD from Mishchenko et al. (2022). The new MNIST experiment uses these same comparators. The comparison reproduced from prior work in Figure 1 is also retained.

E3.justification: The quadratic experiment's stated settings remain unchanged. The added neural experiment introduces a ReLU network configuration and learning rates of 1, 5, and 0.0016 for Ringmaster, Rennala, and Delay-Adaptive ASGD respectively, while retaining 6,174 workers and the preceding worker-time distributions.

E4.justification: The heterogeneous-worker comparison is retained. Figure 3 adds benchmark coverage, but no separate ablation, parameter-sensitivity study, controlled robustness analysis, or error analysis is introduced despite its caption's robustness language.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, error bands, or significance tests. The added experiment follows the existing convergence-curve reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds the first neural-training results, showing Ringmaster reaching the plotted objective floor earlier than Rennala while Delay-Adaptive remains higher. This substantially broadens the empirical findings beyond the quadratic test. Figure 2 also presents revised quadratic convergence trajectories with the same qualitative ordering; the reason for that revision is not documented.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 adds minimization of the runtime bound and explicit worker-time-dependent threshold expressions. New Appendix F derives the initial-point stationarity inequality previously stated in a footnote. The principal assumptions, optimality theorems, and proofs in Appendices A–E remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the claims of optimal asynchronous SGD under fixed and arbitrary computation dynamics, the companion Naive Optimal ASGD method, and empirical superiority. The added experiment supports these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 now distinguishes the computation-time-independent threshold's optimality up to constants from a tighter threshold choice requiring worker-time information. This adds a substantive qualification to the earlier emphasis on speed independence. Existing mechanism explanations and future-work limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The new experiment documents ReLU activation, worker count, reuse of the timing distributions, and plotted algorithm hyperparameters. Its architecture remains ambiguous: Appendix G.1 says 20 layers, while Figure 3 says 2 layers. Existing Python, CPU, simulation, and quadratic tuning details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds LeCun et al. (1998) for MNIST. The Tyurin and MindFlayer reference changes concern matched works' bibliographic information, rather than new research positioning. The relationship to prior asynchronous methods and lower bounds remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 promotes Notations and several run-in method headings to numbered subsections, adds acknowledgments and localized explanations, and renumbers Experiments from Appendix F to G. The main narrative and most wording are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with different colors, markers, legend styling, an explicit seconds label, and a displayed runtime range ending at 2,000 instead of 3,000. Figure 3 is added. Equation display and page flow also change, while Table 1 and the algorithm displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v2 broadens evaluation beyond v1's quadratic experiment and adds useful threshold analysis and an explicit stationarity derivation. These provide limited gains, tempered by the conflicting 20-layer/2-layer descriptions, sparse neural-training details, and unexplained Figure 2 revisions. The central optimality results remain unchanged, so the revision does not establish a substantial overall quality improvement.
